rationale: Uncovered ground: all five earlier rounds took entries from ltp all.txt or gvisor blocklists; the blocked/ext2.txt pool has never been touched, and it holds only two entries (renameat201, renameat202), both renameat2 tests. renameat202 is the tightest possible scope for one localized defect: it is a single assertion that exercises nothing but renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE), verifying the two files' contents and sizes actually swapped. It is enabled in all.txt (so it already passes on ramfs) and blocked only under ext2, which pins the defect to the ext2 backend rather than to the syscall layer or a missing subsystem. The cause is a one-line explicit rejection: kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/impl_for_vfs/inode.rs:220 returns EINVAL for RenameMode::Exchange before doing any work, while ramfs implements the mode (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/fs.rs:1152,1191). The ext2 rename path is already structured to absorb it: Ext2 dir rename() at kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/inode/dir/mod.rs:233 already resolves both the source and the replaced destination inode, locks all participants in ino order via MultiInodeInnerGuards, then validates and applies mutations in separate steps, and a set_entry_target() helper already exists at line 725 - which is what swapping two directory entries' inode targets needs. So this is entry-level bookkeeping in an existing code path, not a feature Asterinas lacks. Host baseline confirms real Linux passes (6/6 TPASS for renameat201, 1/1 TPASS for renameat202, both exit 0, LTP 20260529), so the pool entry reflects an Asterinas gap and not a broken test.
notes: Probed both ext2-pool candidates in one boot on base_commit e8f2b9ca6 (CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/ext2, CONFORMANCE_TEST_SELECTOR=renameat201,renameat202): both fail, 5 passed / 9 failed / 0 broken across the two. kirk reports only per-test pass/fail, so qemu.log carries no per-assertion lines for these. Four measurements appended to select.cache (host pass and probe fail for each). renameat201 stays blocked in this run and shares the same root cause, so it is likely to go green as a side effect of the fix - it is the obvious next round's pick, and its host-pass plus probe-fail records are now cached so the next run need not re-measure. renameat202 also appears in blocked/exfat.txt at line 54; that line is deliberately NOT in pool_entries and must stay, since exfat rejects RENAME_EXCHANGE in its own backend (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/exfat/inode.rs:1659) and this run only enables the ext2 configuration. Deleting the renameat202 line from blocked/ext2.txt leaves that file with one entry (renameat201). renameat202 is already uncommented in all.txt at line 1261, so no all.txt edit is needed. Its runtest entry is 'renameat202 renameat202 -i 10', so it loops 10 times and alternates the swap direction each pass - a fix must be correct in both directions, not just the first. Also note virtiofs rejects RENAME_EXCHANGE the same way (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/virtiofs/inode/mod.rs:466); out of scope here.
